name: OWENS CORNING
business: Makes asphalt roofing shingles, fiberglass and foam insulation, and residential doors, sold to distributors, home centers, contractors and homebuilders in North America and Europe.

events.from: Clarivate Plc (EVP and CFO since Dec 2021); Dana Incorporated (EVP and CFO 2016 to 2021)

events.what: Promoted to President and COO (was EVP, Chief Financial and Operating Officer from 2026-05-01, CFO before that)
New independent director, board expanded from nine to ten
Glass reinforcements divestiture completed (signed 2025-02-13, about $474M estimated price); portfolio now Roofing, Insulation, Doors
events.source: document_id 129698 (IR: 'With the completed divestiture of glass reinforcements'); 10-K via Baba data_profile

events.what: Masonite (Doors) acquisition closed, OUTSIDE the 18-month window; $135M run-rate synergies achieved vs $125M target, plus $75M further structural cost actions identified

next_event.source: No 2026 or 2027 Investor Day found in Baba corpus (lexical search, FY2026). New CFO Collins joins the Q3 2026 earnings call (Chambers, doc 129698, 2026-08-05); call date not in Baba. Last Investor Day was 2025-05-14 (doc 65560).

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Target is 'mid-20s' adjusted EBITDA margin 'on average' with a 20% to 27% range in normal conditions, tied to $12.5B revenue by 2028 under a 1.2M to 1.6M housing starts assumption. Mid-20s taken as 25.0% for the gap math. VA consensus EBITDA is the standardized line, close to company adjusted EBITDA. The $125M Doors synergy target (by May 2026) is already achieved at $135M, so it is not recorded as a forward synergy target.

statements.quote: We have shared our financial targets to achieve $12.5 billion in revenue by 2028 and mid-20s adjusted EBITDA margins, while generating $5 billion in free cash flow and delivering a mid-teens return on capital.
statements.speaker: Todd Fister

statements.quote: Today, we are raising our enterprise guide to a mid-20s EBITDA margin on average, and we expect margins to range between 20% and 27% in normal economic conditions.
statements.speaker: Todd Fister

statements.quote: When we look at the guided Investor Day, we range that based on a housing market between 1.2 million-1.6 million housing starts. We've been at the lower end of that range, both in terms of new starts as well as, resale activity has been fairly weak since we communicated that.
statements.speaker: Todd Fister

statements.quote: When we acquired doors in May 2024, we committed to delivering $125 million of run rate enterprise cost synergies by the end of year two of ownership. As we reach the end of that time period, we have achieved $135 million, exceeding our original commitment. In addition, we've identified another $75 million of structural cost improvements across our operations
statements.speaker: Brian Chambers

street.gap_assumption: December year end, Baba FY labels equal calendar years. Mid-20s read as 25.0% vs VA FY2028 consensus EBITDA margin 21.27% (EBITDA $2.269B on revenue $10.72B). Street FY2028 revenue $10.72B is also well below the $12.5B 2028 target. Management's own 20% to 27% range means 21% is inside the guided band at low housing starts, so the gap is largely a housing-cycle call.
street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (fundamentals, Visible Alpha, fetched 2026-10-01)

evidence_of_progress.note: Order is [Q1 2026, Q2 2026]. Q1 2026 16.3% vs 22.3% (VA). Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin 24% (Chambers and Fister, doc 129698, includes $25M tariff refunds) vs 25.6% in Q2 2025 (VA). VA has not loaded Q2 2026 actuals, so LTM uses Q2 2025 to Q1 2026 (21.1%). Margins are falling, not rising; Q3 2026 carries about $40M net Iran-related cost inflation (Fister). Doors synergies beat target ($135M vs $125M).

verdict: Mechanically high: dated mid-20s by 2028 target, 373 bps above stabilized consensus, plus an external CFO; but CEO is 7 years in, margins are above-peer-cyclical, and the gap is mostly a housing call.
open_questions: Will new CFO Collins reaffirm or reset the 2028 mid-20s margin and $12.5B revenue targets on the Q3 2026 call, given starts at the low end of the 1.2M to 1.6M assumption?
How much of the margin shortfall is price over cost (asphalt, transport, Iran-related inflation) that reverses with price realization versus volume that needs a housing recovery?
Does the $75M of further structural cost work plus Doors margin progress justify a margin path the street is not modeling, independent of housing?
